bounded_slice.candidate: RFC 9530 Content-Digest as a byte-integrity transport field around a canonical JSON evidence package

primary_source.title: RFC 9530: Digest Fields
inspected_sections: 6.1 HTTP Messages Are Not Protected in Full

bounded_slice.tested_scope: Static inspection of exactly one official RFC Editor primary source, RFC 9530, in this invocation. Tested only whether Content-Digest supplies an integrity/digest field contract compatible with canonical JSON evidence bytes. No second public source, implementation execution, external service, protected-primary action, manual-user execution, or scheduler mutation was consumed.
observations: RFC 9530 defines Content-Digest for requests and responses as a Structured Fields Dictionary whose key identifies the hashing algorithm and whose value carries the digest byte output; the digest is calculated over the actual HTTP message content.

The specification states that senders calculate a digest over content and receivers can validate it for integrity, so a canonical JSON evidence package can be byte-bound when its canonical serialization bytes are the HTTP message content used as the digest input.

RFC 9530 is media-type agnostic and explicitly does not define canonicalization for formats such as JSON; its examples note that whitespace affects digest input. Therefore deterministic JSON serialization remains an upstream requirement rather than something supplied by Content-Digest.

Content-Digest protects content integrity but does not protect HTTP fields or provide authentication, authorization, or privacy. An active on-path actor can remove or substitute a digest unless an additional protection mechanism is used.

Because Content-Digest is an HTTP field rather than an intrinsic JSON-package field, offline replay after transport is self-checking only if the digest field (algorithm plus digest value) is preserved together with the exact canonical package bytes; RFC 9530 alone does not define that persistence envelope.
bounded_slice.inference: Within the exact inspected scope, RFC 9530 provides a compatible and precise digest-field contract for binding canonical JSON evidence-package bytes during HTTP transport: canonicalize first, compute the digest over those exact bytes, and preserve algorithm plus digest value. This closes the accidental-corruption/content-byte-integrity child at the transport-envelope level, but it does not close authenticity, malicious substitution/removal resistance, self-contained offline persistence, or canonicalization itself.
bounded_slice.uncertainty: No claim is made that RFC 9530 defines JSON canonicalization, an embedded evidence-package digest property, provenance mapping, uncertainty semantics, replay procedure, or authenticated integrity. No implementation/interoperability behavior was executed or tested.
bounded_slice.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_us: 0 for the specification-level digest contract inspected here; concrete persistence/replay/authentication and remaining schema mapping are separate unresolved children and are not claimed solved.
bounded_slice.quota_zero_assessment: The RFC is a public static standard and the inspected digest-field mechanism is algorithmic/local; no hosted compute, paid API, monthly/trial credit, or external execution is required by the contract itself. No implementation cost/quota claim beyond this specification-level scope is made.
